reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh taking direct action to help the Hebrew people: (1) God instructs Moses to command the Israelites where to position themselves, (2) God explicitly orders Moses to part the sea so the Israelites can cross through on dry ground ('וְיָבֹאוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם בַּיַּבָּשָׁה'), (3) God parts the sea using a strong east wind, enabling their safe passage, and (4) God closes the waters over the pursuing Egyptians, ensuring the Israelites' escape. While the text also emphasizes that glorifying Yahweh's name among the Egyptians is another significant divine goal ('וְיָדְעוּ מִצְרַיִם כִּי־ אֲנִי יְהוָה'), helping the Hebrew people is clearly one of Yahweh's demonstrated goals in this passage, even if not the sole focus.
story: The Parting of the Red Sea
